passages.title: Questions 111–120
passages.body: (111) _____ by the charm of Nature around him, man has expressed his appreciation of it in works of art produced by him. This goes back to a time (112) _____ he was still a primitive being. Art (113) _____ a softening influence on him. The earliest paintings of the prehistoric age in the caves all over the world give us magnificent examples of the (114) _____ eye and the trained hand in man's savage state. The colours chosen, the movement (115) _____ and the expressions the pictures are (116) _____ with really make us marvel, even if all of them are not of the (117) _____ of the paintings at Altamira. The prehistoric cave paintings in India give us a picture of life in those (118) _____ days of the early man in India. It is a great and true experience that Kalidasa expresses, when he feels that (119) _____ the happiest man feels (120) _____ when he sees beautiful things or hears melodious notes.
passages.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

The officer under suspension felt __intimated__ by the committee members during his interrogation regarding the allegations against him.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Intimated vs intimidated.
Step 1: Being questioned about allegations makes one feel frightened, i.e. intimidated.
Step 2: 'Intimated' means hinted or announced, so it does not fit.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

Amongst them all, she was the only one with the __perquisite__ to understand the complexity of the situation.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Perquisite vs perspicacity.
Step 1: A perquisite is a benefit given with a job. The sentence needs a quality of mind to understand a complex situation: perspicacity (keen insight).
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

At the official function organised for the attending dignitaries, guests arrived in __scrumptious__ attire for the banquet.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Scrumptious describes food, not clothes.
Step 1: Rich, splendid attire is 'sumptuous'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

The lake atop the mountain has always been the __lyre__ for intrepid hikers.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Lyre is a musical instrument.
Step 1: The lake attracts hikers, so it is a 'lure'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

The candidates went through an intensive __instruction__ process before their absorption into the service.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Induction.
Step 1: A process that brings new recruits into a service is induction.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

The office memorandum directed personnel to __minimise__ their consumption of office stationery by up to twenty percent.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Minimise means reduce to the smallest possible amount.
Step 1: 'Minimise ... by up to twenty percent' is a contradiction, since minimise cannot be partial. The best correction is 'reduce'.
Answer: (d).

Note: This question has been lightly edited from the printed paper for clarity and a single defensible answer.
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

The announcement of an unexpected bonus led to great __tumult__ among the staff.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The sentence describes a happy event.
Step 1: Tumult means noisy confusion. An unexpected bonus would cause merriment (happiness). 'Uproar' and 'upheaval' repeat the idea of disorder.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

The __scurrilous__ remarks in the article were met with great joy by the leadership of the company.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Scurrilous remarks are abusive.
Step 1: Leaders would not meet abuse with joy, so the word that improves the sentence is 'laudatory' (praising).
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

His inappropriate behaviour earned __plaudits__ from his colleagues.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Plaudits are praises.
Step 1: Inappropriate behaviour earns criticism, i.e. opprobrium (public disgrace).
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

The __enormity__ of the mountain range stunned the visitors to the hill station.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Enormity means great wickedness; enormousness means great size.
Step 1: A mountain range's size is its enormousness.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The accusation of abatement to the crime__ (a) __that had been levelled at him__ (b) __was eventually not proven in court.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Abatement vs abetment.
Step 1: Abatement means reduction. Helping to commit a crime is 'abetment'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The unintentional mistakes__ (a) __made by the clerical staff__ (b) __was overlooked by the officer.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Subject-verb agreement.
Step 1: The subject 'mistakes' is plural, so the verb should be 'were overlooked'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The opening batsman was famous__ (a) __for the imperial strokes__ (b) __he played on the cricket field.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Check each part.
Step 1: 'famous for the imperial strokes he played' is acceptable ('imperial' = majestic). The printed word 'stokes' is a typo for 'strokes'.
Step 2: There is no real error.
Answer: (d).

Note: This question has been lightly edited from the printed paper for clarity and a single defensible answer.
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Each student was meant to receive__ (a) __an equal share of the scholarship but the eventual distribution__ (b) __was found to be iniquitous.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Check each part.
Step 1: 'Each student ... an equal share ... was found to be iniquitous (unfair)' is grammatically correct.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__No one turned up__ (a) __to claim the stowed away piece of baggage__ (b) __which was discovered on the luggage compartment of the bus.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Preposition 'in' for a compartment.
Step 1: Baggage is discovered 'in' the luggage compartment, not 'on' it.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Certain animals have a tendency__ (a) __to communicate only with__ (b) __its own species and none other.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Pronoun agreement.
Step 1: 'Animals' is plural, so use 'their own species', not 'its'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__As soon as the clock__ (a) __chimed to announce the hour at midnight__ (b) __she sprung up from her bed.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Past tense of spring.
Step 1: The past tense is 'sprang'. 'Sprung' is the past participle.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__There are people who are likely__ (a) __to fraternise with their__ (b) __own community yet none other.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Check each part.
Step 1: 'people who are likely to fraternise with their own community yet none other' is grammatically correct.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The mime show attracted__ (a) __a huge audience despite the high price of tickets__ (b) __which defied the purpose of the public event.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Check each part.
Step 1: The sentence is correct.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__He was unable to recall__ (a) __where he had hanged his shirt__ (b) __after returning home from office.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Hang has two past forms.
Step 1: For clothes and objects, the past tense is 'hung'. 'Hanged' is used for execution.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

There is no truth in ______ claims even though they have been cleverly stated.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A determiner is needed.
Step 1: 'these claims' points to the claims mentioned.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

The bridge was intended to allow people to cross ______ to the other side of the river and get to work.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Phrasal verb.
Step 1: 'cross over to the other side' is the natural phrase; 'across' would repeat the idea.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

I shall not rest ______ I have gone to the bottom of this matter and found the truth.
questions.explanation:
Concept: 'Until' shows the time up to which the action continues.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

There are several reasons behind my choice of location ______ the family visit.
questions.explanation:
Concept: 'Choice of location for the family visit' - for shows purpose.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

All human beings ought to have a moral centre to fall back ______ in times of crisis.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Phrasal verb 'fall back on' = rely on.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the sentences in which the underlined word has been used correctly.

Words: Pare, Pair, Pear
1. It is important to __pare__ the branches of a tree to prevent excessive growth.
2. The __pair__ of trees looked identical from a distance.
3. The __pear__ tree was revered by the children of the locality for the bounty it offered each year.
In which of the sentences given above has/have the words been used correctly ?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Pare = trim; pair = two; pear = fruit.
Step 1: All three are used correctly.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the sentences in which the underlined word has been used correctly.

Words: Séance, Sconce, Scone
1. Those who practise spiritualism are at times seen to participate in a __séance__.
2. They enjoyed eating the __sconce__ that were served to them in the exclusive club.
3. The __scone__ reading on the graph indicated the correct value output of the experiment.
In which of the sentences given above has/have the words been used correctly ?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Séance = meeting to contact spirits; sconce = wall light holder; scone = baked item; score = points.
Step 1: 1 is correct. 2 should be 'scones'. 3 should be 'score reading'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the sentences in which the underlined word has been used correctly.

Words: Truism, Altruism
1. That one has to reap what one sows is a __truism__.
2. The __altruism__ uttered by the seer covered the higher levels of spiritual knowledge.
In which of the sentences given above has/have the words been used correctly ?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Truism = obvious truth; altruism = selfless concern for others.
Step 1: 1 is correct. 2 does not fit; wisdom or sermon is meant.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the sentences in which the underlined word has been used correctly.

Words: Consequent, Consequence
1. __Consequent__ to the decisions taken by the committee a new set of procedures was brought into force.
2. The past is of little __consequence__ when one is willing to bravely face the challenges of the future.
In which of the sentences given above has/have the words been used correctly ?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Consequent = following as a result; consequence = result or importance.
Step 1: 1 'Consequent to the decisions' is accepted in formal Indian usage. 2 'of little consequence' is correct.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the sentences in which the underlined word has been used correctly.

Words: Seize, Cease, Crease
1. The customs department decided to __seize__ the consignment of contraband goods.
2. To improve relations the two parties decided that the hostilities between them should __cease__.
3. Military personnel are required to be attired in trousers with a knife-edge-like __crease__.
In which of the sentences given above has/have the words been used correctly ?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Seize = take hold of; cease = stop; crease = fold line.
Step 1: All three sentences are correct.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Listen with half an ear
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: To listen with half an ear is to listen without paying full attention.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Dyed in the wool
questions.opt_a: Changing notions because of a fluffy mind
questions.opt_d: Unchanging and firm in belief and conviction
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: Wool was dyed before weaving so the colour stays; so 'dyed in the wool' is fixed in belief.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Let sleeping dogs lie
questions.opt_a: Let things remain as they are because of laziness
questions.opt_b: Not interfere in situations where interference may exacerbate matters
questions.explanation:
Concept: Proverb.
Step 1: Do not disturb a situation that may become worse.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

A stitch in time saves nine
questions.opt_a: Tying up complex matters with clever manoeuvres
questions.opt_b: Poking at something repeatedly to rescue a situation
questions.opt_c: Making unlikely connections among disparate subjects
questions.opt_d: Timely addressal of a problem prevents future exacerbation of the same
questions.explanation:
Concept: Proverb.
Step 1: One timely stitch saves nine later; fix problems early.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Fight fire with fire
questions.opt_a: Use the same force or strategy of one's opponent to counter them
questions.opt_b: Use incendiary tactics to destroy by fire
questions.opt_c: Add fuel to further escalate a fiery situation
questions.opt_d: Scorch one's opponent with a barrage of firing
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: Use the same methods as your opponent against them.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Straight and narrow
questions.opt_b: Honest and morally acceptable way of being
questions.opt_c: Follow the straight path defined by society
questions.opt_d: To not deviate from one's goal
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: The 'straight and narrow' is an honest, morally correct way of life.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Someone's ears are burning
questions.opt_a: The feeling when someone thinks others are talking about them
questions.opt_c: Being angry due to unfair criticism
questions.opt_d: Itching to enter into an argument
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: When others talk about you, your ears are said to burn.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Turn one's stomach
questions.opt_a: Being nauseated by something or someone
questions.opt_b: Being plagued by a stomach upset
questions.opt_c: Unable to cope with the changes
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: Something that turns your stomach makes you feel sick.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

The world is your oyster
questions.opt_a: You have all the opportunity to obtain what you wish from life
questions.opt_c: Life is a puzzle you cannot ever unravel
questions.opt_d: The world will dazzle you if you are not careful
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: If the world is your oyster, all opportunities are open to you.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Cast one's bread upon the waters
questions.opt_b: To do good without seeking reward
questions.opt_c: To while away one's time in unfruitful activity
questions.opt_d: To misdirect one's efforts in life
questions.explanation:
Concept: Biblical idiom.
Step 1: Casting bread upon the waters means doing good without expecting a reward.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: The snowy albatross is among the largest birds that fly in the world.
S2: It has the widest wingspan among all birds, with lengths reaching up to 12 feet.
The second statement :
questions.explanation:
Concept: Confirms = supports the first statement with facts.
Step 1: S2 gives facts (widest wingspan up to 12 feet) that support S1.
Answer: (c).

Note: This question has been lightly edited from the printed paper for clarity and a single defensible answer.
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: A scientific theory is first proposed as a hypothesis.
S2: After it is subjected to inquiry and is proven, it becomes a thesis.
The second statement :
questions.explanation:
Concept: Extends = continues the idea.
Step 1: S1 says a theory begins as a hypothesis; S2 describes the next step. So S2 extends S1.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: The manhunt for the perpetrator of the crime spread across the entire state.
S2: There was deep public anger triggered by the enormity of the crime.
The second statement :
questions.opt_a: is a precursor to the first
questions.opt_d: alters the premise of the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: Precursor = comes before.
Step 1: The public anger caused by the crime came before the manhunt spread.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: Awareness about one's own personality type is very important.
S2: Self-awareness is a difficult goal for most people.
The second statement :
questions.explanation:
Concept: Contrapuntal = offering a contrasting point that goes with the main one.
Step 1: S1 says self-awareness is important; S2 says it is hard to achieve. S2 does not deny S1 but sets a counterpoint.
Answer: (b).

Note: This question has been lightly edited from the printed paper for clarity and a single defensible answer.
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: Liberalisation changed the contours of India's economy.
S2: India is today poised to become one of the top economies of the world.
The second statement :
questions.explanation:
Concept: Correlates = is connected with.
Step 1: India's rise is connected to liberalisation.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: The final outcome can never be predicted incontrovertibly.
S2: All outcomes are based on variables that cannot always be fully understood.
The second statement :
questions.opt_b: reinforces the first to an extent
questions.opt_d: definitely does not follow the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: Judge how strongly S2 supports S1.
Step 1: S1 says outcomes can never be predicted for certain. S2 says outcomes rest on variables that cannot always be fully understood, a weaker claim.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: Mastery over any art form requires years of dedication and perseverance.
S2: It takes 10,000 hours of practice to become an expert in a field.
The second statement :
questions.opt_a: is not consistent with the first
questions.opt_b: is fully consistent with the first
questions.opt_c: is marginally consistent with the first
questions.opt_d: is the only possible explanation for the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: Consistency.
Step 1: Years of dedication fits the idea of 10,000 hours of practice.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: The beauty of India's democracy rests in the greatness of its Constitution.
S2: The Constitution of India upholds the collective values of the country's civilizational ethos.
The second statement :
questions.opt_a: connects with the mention of Indian democracy in the first
questions.opt_b: provides a reason for the assertion regarding the Constitution in the first
questions.opt_c: contradicts the assertion about democracy in the first
questions.opt_d: has no connection with the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: Reason.
Step 1: S2 explains why the Constitution is great (it upholds shared values), supporting S1's claim.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: Roseate is an adjective for the rose flower.
S2: The rose is a powerful poetic symbol in many languages.
The second statement :
questions.explanation:
Concept: Expands = adds to the idea.
Step 1: S2 adds more about the rose as a symbol.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: The early bird gets the worm.
S2: To go about one's tasks expeditiously is to achieve one's goals.
The second statement :
questions.opt_b: provides a metaphorical reassertion of the first
questions.opt_c: reinforces the assumption of the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: Metaphor.
Step 1: 'Early bird' is a metaphor; S2 restates it in plain words.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2025 English set A (set code CEBN-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:

questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The minimum thermometer has a large bore and its fluid is colourless alcohol.
S6: The daily temperature is recorded since a permanent, continuous record of temperature is desired.
P: When the meniscus moves up the bore it leaves the index behind to register the lowest temperature.
Q: Resetting the dumbbell of the minimum thermometer is accompanied by the action of inverting the stem until the index slides down to the meniscus.
R: A tiny, dark index in the shape of a long dumbbell is placed in the bore below the top of the alcohol column.
S: It is mounted horizontally and as the alcohol contracts with the decreasing temperature the meniscus of the alcohol pulls the index down.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Describe the instrument, then how it works.
Step 1: S1 introduces the minimum thermometer. S says it is mounted horizontally and the meniscus pulls the index down as the alcohol contracts. R describes the tiny index. Q tells how it is reset. P describes the index staying behind as the meniscus rises.
Step 2: S6 ends with daily recording.
Answer: (d) SRQP.

questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The Cretaceous Period extends from about 146 million years ago to 65 million years ago.
S6: During this period, enormous quantity of basaltic lava was poured out to the surface assuming a great thickness of over three thousand meters.
P: Apart from deposits this period is marked by the transgression of the sea and outpouring of huge quantity of lava so as to form the Deccan trap and intrusion of plutonic rocks such as gabbro and granite.
Q: Towards the end of the Cretaceous Period the peninsula was affected by intense volcanic activity.
R: This outpouring has been very widely distributed in the country with divergent facies of deposits being found in different parts of India.
S: In contrast to the relatively newer Himalayas, these facies that are found in different parts of India are much older in origin.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Period features, then the lava, then its distribution.
Step 1: S1 gives the dates. P gives the period's features, including lava outpouring (Deccan trap). R: 'This outpouring' is widely distributed. S compares the facies with the Himalayas. Q: towards the end, intense volcanic activity. S6: during this period, lava poured out.
Answer: (c) PRSQ.

Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Drought is a continuous and lengthy period during which no significant rainfall is recorded during the rainy season.
S6: In India, droughts are more frequent in the areas where the average annual rainfall is less than 60 cm and the variability of rainfall is over 20 per cent.
P: This definition however, does not apply to Mawsynram and Cherrapunji, where even one week recording less than 0.25 mm of rainfall may be considered as a drought period.
Q: In general, the areas recording less than 60 cm of rainfall annually and in which the variability of rainfall is more than 20 per cent are the drought prone areas in India.
R: In India, the Meteorological Department has defined drought as a period of at least 22 consecutive days on none of which is there more than 0.25 mm of rainfall.
S: Areas where the variability of rainfall varies between 20 to 60 per cent are the chronic drought prone areas.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Definition, exception, general area.
Step 1: S1 defines drought generally. R gives the IMD definition. P: 'This definition however' does not apply to Mawsynram. Q: in general, areas with less than 60 cm. S: chronic areas. S6 summarises.
Answer: (d) RPQS.

R: For example, a farmer having 10 acres in Kerala is a large farmer, while in Rajasthan, Punjab and Haryana he falls under the category of a small or medium farmer.
S: All the studies conducted in areas where Green Revolution is a success show that the large farmers have been the main gainers of the package programme.

S1: The __moribund__ state of the decaying colony depressed everyone.
S2: The strength of the collective remained __moribund__ despite attempts at scuttling unity.
S3: Driven by a common purpose, the __moribund__ group decided it would prevail notwithstanding of the adverseness of the situation.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Moribund = near death, declining.
Step 1: S1 (decaying colony) is correct. S2 and S3 use it for a strong, united group, which is wrong.
Answer: (a) 1.

Directions: Decide how many of the three sentences use the underlined word correctly: (a) 1, (b) 2, (c) 3, (d) none.

S1: The Gangetic plains are blessed with historically-significant __fecundity__ on account of its rich soil.
S2: The couple sought blessings at the temple that was believed to possess the power to transform childlessness into __fecundity__.
S3: The grass across the prairies made the landscape appear particularly __fecund__, with cattle grazing by the thousands.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Fecundity = fertility; fecund = fertile.
Step 1: S1 (rich soil), S2 (childlessness to fertility) and S3 (fertile landscape) are all correct.
Answer: (c) 3.

questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best describes the meaning of both words.

Ensure and Insure
questions.opt_a: Ensure is a transitive verb meaning to make something certain. Insure is a transitive verb meaning to make certain by taking necessary precaution.
questions.opt_b: Ensure is a determiner meaning to make something certain. Insure is a determiner meaning to make certain by taking necessary precaution.
questions.opt_c: Ensure is a determiner meaning to make certain by taking necessary precaution. Insure is a determiner to make something certain.

Insuperable

questions.opt_b: The group went insuperable for weeks during the agitation until the demands were met.
questions.opt_c: The insuperable element in the whole engagement was the leader herself.
questions.opt_d: The hostel administration remained insuperable for a month.

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Only one sentence uses the word correctly. Choose it.

Amoral
questions.opt_a: Murder can be categorized as an amoral act.
questions.opt_b: We must send out a message that we are not an immoral society.
questions.opt_c: It is amoral to cheat the one who loves you.
questions.opt_d: The pursuit of victory at all costs allows for amoral conduct.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Amoral = lacking any sense of right and wrong (not immoral).
Step 1: 'Murder', 'cheating' are immoral, not amoral. 'Pursuit of victory at all costs allows for amoral conduct' means conduct that ignores morals, which is correct.
Answer: (d).

questions.opt_b: The family decided to emigrate to a safe and secure country.
questions.opt_c: Workers emigrate from province to province in search of seasonal jobs.

questions.explanation:

Answer: (b).
